# `opense4.ai`

Computer players (docs/MODDING_SDK.md, section 6; docs/sdk/ai-protocol.md).

A computer player is a subclass of `Player` that overrides the decisions it wants to make; every one it leaves alone is the classic AI's:

```python
from opense4 import ai, cmd, order

class Admiral(ai.Player):
    def orders(self, view, orders):
        for fleet in view.my.idle_fleets:
            target = view.galaxy.nearest(fleet, view.enemy_colonies)
            if target is not None:
                orders.add(cmd.give(fleet, [order.attack(object=target.planet)]))
        orders.extend(ai.builtin.orders(view, skip=["attack"]))
```

`ai.builtin` (opense4.builtin) is the classic AI as a library.

Source: [python/opense4/ai.py](../../../python/opense4/ai.py). Index: [the API reference](README.md).

Contents: [`Orders`](#orders), [`TacticalOrders`](#tacticalorders), [`ColonyTypeQuestion`](#colonytypequestion), [`EntryQuestion`](#entryquestion), [`DecloakQuestion`](#decloakquestion), [`Piece`](#piece), [`BattleState`](#battlestate), [`Player`](#player).

## `TacticalOrders`

```python
TacticalOrders(empire: int)
```

Extends `Orders`.

The tactical orders a battle round gives (docs/sdk/commands.md, "Tactical battles"), each for the player's side: opense4.tactical builds them, and `empire` is filled in.

### `TacticalOrders.add`

```python
add(command: Dict[str, Any]) -> None
```

### `TacticalOrders.fire`

```python
fire(piece: Any, target: Any, weapon: int = -1) -> None
```

Fires a piece's weapon (every enabled one: -1) at a target piece.

### `TacticalOrders.move`

```python
move(piece: Any, x: int, y: int) -> None
```

Moves a piece toward a square.

`TacticalOrders.target` is `TacticalOrders.fire`.


|---|---|---|

| `planet_id` | `Optional[int]` |  |

## `Player`

A computer player. Override the callbacks you want; the others are the classic AI's.

Set for every request: `empire_id`, `turn`, `call`, `seed`, `random` (an opense4.rng.Random seeded from the request, the same every time the request is replayed), `view` (the session's latest view), `refused` (the commands of the previous planning call the game refused: [{index, command, reason}]). `memory` is what the player keeps between sessions (a map at first): only plain values (None, bool, int, str, lists, dicts with str keys).

| Attribute | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `memory` | `Any` | `None` |  |
| `empire_id` | `int` | `-1` |  |
| `turn` | `int` | `0` |  |
| `call` | `str` | `""` |  |
| `seed` | `int` | `0` |  |
| `random` | `Random` |  |  |
| `view` | `Any` | `None` |  |
| `refused` | `List[Dict[str, Any]]` | `[]` |  |

| Property | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `rules` | `Any` | The rules view (opense4.rules.Rules), asked once per session. |

### `Player.politics`

```python
politics(view: Any, orders: Orders) -> Any
```

Start of the turn, before messages are delivered: diplomacy. Default: the classic Politics minister.

### `Player.orders`

```python
orders(view: Any, orders: Orders) -> Any
```

Start of the turn, after politics and delivery: movement, colonizing, attack, defence, exploration, fleets, supply, scrapping, refits. Default: the classic ministers.

### `Player.economy`

```python
economy(view: Any, orders: Orders) -> Any
```

End of the turn: designs, research, intelligence, construction. Default: the classic ministers.

### `Player.colony_type`

```python
colony_type(view: Any, question: ColonyTypeQuestion) -> Optional[str]
```

A colony is founded: return one of `question.choices`, or None for the classic choice.

### `Player.enter_sector`

```python
enter_sector(view: Any, question: EntryQuestion) -> Optional[bool]
```

A move would enter a sector with enemies: True to enter, False to stay out, None to enter.

### `Player.decloak`

```python
decloak(view: Any, question: DecloakQuestion) -> Optional[bool]
```

A cloaked vehicle or colony needs to decloak: True, False, or None for the classic minister.

### `Player.battle_round`

```python
battle_round(battle: BattleState, orders: TacticalOrders) -> Any
```

A round of a space battle: add tactical orders for our pieces, or none to let the strategies decide.

### `Player.end_session`

```python
end_session() -> None
```

The session ends: the last chance to update `memory`.

### `Player.note`

```python
note(obj: Any, text: str, kind: Optional[str] = None) -> None
```

Attaches a note to something on the map for the client's AI view: a Vehicle, Fleet, Colony, SpaceObject, System, Empire, Design or Message, or an id with its `kind` ("vehicle", "fleet", "object", "system", "empire", "design", "message"). A later note on the same thing this turn replaces it.

### `Player.log`

```python
log(text: Any) -> None
```

Writes a line to the game's log file (not the empire's in-game log).

### `Player.query`

```python
query(name: str, **args: Any) -> Any
```

Asks a query of docs/sdk/view.md ("Queries") now (see opense4.services.query).

### `Player.apply`

```python
apply(command: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any
```

Applies a command now, in a planning call, and returns the engine's answer: `result.ok`, `result.reason` (docs/sdk/ai-protocol.md, section 6). A command applied this way is not also given in the call's answer.
